name: nbind
listed_description: Magical headers that make your C++ library accessible from JavaScript.
reason: No benchmark or performance number against any baseline. README (opened) only says copying data across the language boundary is costly and simple calculations are faster in JavaScript; its Alternatives section (Embind, v8pp, node-ffi and others) has no timings, and a WebSearch for nbind vs nan / node-addon-api benchmarks found none. Last commit 2019-05-04, MIT, about 2.0k stars.

name: SIP
listed_description: C or C++ Bindings Generator for Python v2 and v3.
reason: No numbers in the project README or docs/introduction.rst (opened on github.com/Python-SIP/sip via raw.githubusercontent.com). Only anecdotes from PyQt mailing-list posts (seen in WebSearch snippets, riverbankcomputing.com unreachable here): a user porting from SWIG reported source about 40% smaller and 'noticeably higher framerates', unquantified; SIP creates class methods lazily. No benchmark against SWIG, pybind11, Boost.Python or Cython found. BSD-2-Clause.

name: V7
reason: README claims small size (40k-120k static, 800 bytes RAM at init with freeze) and makes no speed claim; no benchmark in README, ReleaseNotes.md or the javascript-zoo engine page. The only speed number found is a javascript-zoo-data CI result where V7 (gcc 16.1.0 build, git ce5212ae) scores Richards 4.944 versus QuickJS 746 and Duktape 396 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ivankra/javascript-zoo-data/data/bench/amd64/cesanta-v7.json), i.e. far slower. Deprecated in favour of mJS; last commit 2020-11-30; GPL-2.0 or commercial.
